price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent second-half change
regression to the mean in H2 suppression
methodological_questions: What share of between-team variance in opponents' H2-H1 change is signal rather than noise, given 120 team-seasons?
Does the defense effect persist across seasons and across random halves of the same season?
How should regression to the mean, garbage time, opponent H2-H1 tendency and game state be handled?
What permutation baseline defines 'no team trait'?

historical_evidence.finding: First-half play-type reliance did not predict second-half suppression after controlling for H1 PPP and mean reversion. Matched ATT did not survive BH correction. Lift over the mean-reversion baseline was only +0.039 (0.550 vs 0.511). The record states that the bulk of H2 suppression is RTM. n=8873 team-games; recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null).

Season-to-season stability of star-level top suppressors was low: only 2/30 (7%) met the 75% same-top-suppressor rule (30 stars x 4 seasons, min n=20 per cell). This is player-level and play-type-level, not team H2-H1 change.
Series-level AVOID share vs winning gave rho=-0.26, p=0.07 (n=50 series), underpowered (~80 series needed) and still confounded by team quality.
Inferred scheme labels could not separate real defensive adjustment from the offense executing differently. Transition matrices were near-uniform, consistent with label noise.
The apparent A1 adapter PPP lift was attributed to a construction, selection or labelling flaw. The recorded limitations are label error and selection/regression to the mean.
Play-type label backfill verification ended with Final: FAIL (PNR share out of band, team identity check failed, near-zero PULL_UP shares for many teams in 2024-25).
Descriptive team BEST/AVOID shares (AVOID% 6.8%-50.6%). There was no outcome test, and player samples were small.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating H2 suppression after heavy H1 usage as a real effect
failed_approaches.why: Mostly regression to the mean. Matched effects did not survive BH correction and added little over the mean-reversion baseline.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred defensive scheme labels to measure adjustment
failed_approaches.why: Label noise. Adjustment cannot be separated from offensive execution (A_unanswerable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Interpreting the adapter PPP lift as a coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Artifact from selection, regression to the mean and label error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level association between AVOID share and winning
failed_approaches.why: n=50 was underpowered and the association was confounded by team quality.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Assuming stable per-star suppressor identity across seasons

evidence_establishes: Earlier H2-suppression work found that much of the apparent H2 suppression is mean reversion (FAM:SF-APPS-070, rejected).
Related stability tests (top suppressor per star, FAM:SF-APPA-058) were null across seasons.
Labelled or inferred play-type and scheme variables in this project are unreliable (FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPA-001), so a reliability test should not rest on them.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record directly tests the reliability (split-half or cross-season) of a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change.
Nothing retrieved shows a team-level H2-H1 trait is absent. The nulls concern play-type usage and star-level suppressors, not team-level score-based H2-H1 change.
No retrieved record gives variance components or an ICC for team-level H2-H1 change.
own_inferences: The H2-H1 difference is a noisy difference score. A team-season of about 82 games gives a standard error plausibly larger than any true between-team spread, so reliability is probably low (to be verified, not recorded).
Regression to the mean mechanically produces negative H1-to-H2 correlation. A naive split on an H1-defined subset would show spurious 'effects' and spurious persistence.
Defense and opponent are confounded: opponent offense has its own H2-H1 tendency, and the defense's own offense shapes score state and substitution patterns, so opponent random effects are needed.
Using only score-derived H1/H2 efficiency from PBP avoids the label-error issues that sank the inferred-label families.
Most likely outcome is a small or null variance component, with some cross-season persistence driven by pace, rotation and coaching patterns rather than 'suppression'.
uncertainties: Whether the 120 units are 30 teams x 4 seasons, and whether the partial 2025-26 data matter (the data state as of 2026-10-06 appears complete).
The true between-team SD of the H2-H1 effect is unknown, so the achievable reliability is unknown.
Whether the definition of 'effect' (points per 100 possessions, margin, or a specific play type) matters for the result.
Records were truncated ('cut'), and I did not read the full text of FAM:SF-APPS-070.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved nulls and artifacts raised my prior that apparent H2-H1 effects are RTM or label artifacts. They moved the plan toward a score-based, label-free variance-components design with permutation nulls and explicit RTM controls, instead of a naive correlation test. They did not make the question unanswerable, because no prior record tested team-level reliability directly.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 120 team-seasons (about 90 consecutive-season pairs, non-independent). Only fairly large true between-team variance is detectable. A null would be 'not detectable', not 'absent'.
The H2-H1 difference score has large game-level noise. Split-half reliability may be low by construction.

prior_work.summary: Adjacent work (H1 usage predicting H2 suppression, star suppressor stability) was null or dominated by RTM. Label-based adaptation work was artifact or untestable. The specific question of team-level reliability of a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change was not retrieved as tested.

risks.text: H2-H1 change is negatively tied to H1 level. Without conditioning on H1 level, a defense's apparent effect and its persistence are confounded by mean reversion.
Noisy difference scores with about 82 games per team-season. Reliability must be estimated with variance components and Spearman-Brown correction, not raw correlation.
Opponent offense identity and H2-H1 tendency, the defense team's own offense, score state and garbage time, rest, home/away, and coaching and rotation patterns.
120 team-seasons gives wide CIs on ICC and cross-season r. Consecutive-season pairs share teams and are non-independent.
Rosters, coaches and league scoring and pace change across seasons, which depresses cross-season persistence independent of a true trait.
Several outcome definitions (ORtg, margin, eFG) and subsets could be run. Only one primary is allowed.
Do not define the defense effect using the same games used to test persistence. Keep split-half sets disjoint.
Avoid inferred play-type or scheme labels. The primary analysis should use only PBP score and possession counts.

design.estimand: Between-team variance component (ICC) of the defensive team's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change in points per 100 possessions, after adjusting for opponent offense, H1 level, venue and score-state. Secondary: cross-season correlation of team-season effects and Spearman-Brown corrected split-half reliability.
design.unit: Team-season (defense) for reliability. Underlying data are team-games (defense x opponent) with H1 and H2 opponent points per 100 possessions.
design.sample: All 120 team-seasons from 2022-23 to 2025-26, regular season only for the primary analysis (playoffs are too few games per team and selected). Exclude overtime and possessions in garbage time (pre-registered score margin and clock threshold, e.g. margin >=25 in Q4). Report a sensitivity analysis without the exclusion.
design.power: Before looking at outcomes, compute the minimum detectable ICC from the game-level residual SD of H2-H1 change (about 82 games per team-season) via simulation. State that 120 units (about 90 consecutive-season pairs) can detect only a true team SD of roughly 0.5-1 point per 100 possessions or more (to be confirmed by simulation). A null is reported as 'trait variance below the MDE', not as absence.
design.controls: Mixed model: opponent H2-H1 change ~ H1 opponent level (RTM), home/away, rest, opponent random effect (offense identity and own tendency), season fixed effect, defense team random effect. Report the ICC with a parametric bootstrap or cluster CI. Cross-season: correlate team-season random-effect estimates (empirical Bayes shrunk) for consecutive seasons, with a cluster bootstrap by team. Also split-half (odd/even games) reliability within each season.
design.falsification: Permutation null: shuffle the defense-team labels across games within season, and shuffle H1/H2 labels within game, to build the null ICC and cross-season r distribution. Placebo outcome: use H1-only or H2-only opponent efficiency, where a defense trait is expected to appear, to confirm that the pipeline detects a known stable trait. Negative control: a nonsense pairing of teams across seasons.
design.multiplicity: One primary: the ICC of the defense random effect on points per 100 possessions. Secondary outcomes (eFG, turnover share, margin) are labeled exploratory with BH correction. No subgroup or play-type analyses.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the ICC lower 95% CI > 0.02 and exceeds the permutation 95th percentile, and cross-season r of shrunk effects > 0.2 with CI excluding 0, and the result survives the garbage-time sensitivity analysis. Rejected if the ICC upper CI < 0.05 and the MDE is below the effect of practical interest. Otherwise inconclusive. If the effect vanishes after conditioning on H1 level, label it an RTM artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API PBP and box-score files for 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons (complete as of 2026-04-13). Freeze file hashes and the exclusion rules before analysis. No inferred play-type labels used.

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent second-half change
methodological_questions: Is a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across seasons (split-half or season-to-season reliability)?
How much of the team-level H2-H1 effect is noise versus signal given 120 team-seasons?
How to control for regression to the mean, score-state/garbage-time confounding, and opponent strength?
What placebo or permutation baselines are needed to test reliability?
args.query: Reliability of a defense's effect on opponents' second-half minus first-half change as a persistent team trait, using team-seasons from 2022-23 to 2025-26

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull the full text of FAM:SF-APPS-070, but I think my budget allows it and I can reasonably finish without it. The evidence so far shows no record directly tests whether team-level reliability of a defense changes an opponent's H2-H1 figure, so I'm starting to put that gap into the answer.

I'm settling the verdicts on the remaining records: the RTM explanation holds for the H2 suppression, the season-stability check fails, and several others are untestable or underpowered. Next I'm sizing the design, with 120 team-seasons and a low expected reliability, and starting to frame the estimand.

I'm laying out the design now: a split-half reliability check on odd and even games, with a permutation null and a random-effects model for each defense's effect on opponent H2-H1 change. I'm setting the decision thresholds on ICC, Spearman-Brown reliability and cross-season correlation, and attaching rough probabilities to each verdict, leaning toward proceeding with changes.

The evidence so far shows no record directly tests whether team-level reliability of a defense changes an opponent's H2-H1 figure, so I'm starting to put that gap into the answer.

I'm settling the verdicts on the remaining records: the RTM explanation holds for the H2 suppression, the season-stability check fails, and several others are untestable or underpowered. Next I'm sizing the design, with 120 team-seasons and a low expected reliability, and starting to frame the estimand.

I'm laying out the design now: a split-half reliability check on odd and even games, with a permutation null and a random-effects model for each defense's effect on opponent H2-H1 change. I'm setting the decision thresholds on ICC, Spearman-Brown reliability and cross-season correlation, and attaching rough probabilities to each verdict, leaning toward proceeding with changes.
